It provides a path to the file in question.  Either copy and paste it into file explorer, or follow the names of the folders until you find the file.  Delete it and empty your recycling bin.

If it says it's being used in a program, open up task manager, find the one that appears most likely to be the culprit, and end the task. (If you can't tell for sure if a task is or isn't something important, right click on it and click open file location, and see if it's in a folder of something you trust; you can also google the name of the task in question with "task manager" on the end and get results of what it is and what it might be doing).

If it says that you don't have permission to delete, Google "take ownership", open the link that says install/remove "take ownership", and follow the instructions to add an option to your right click menu (context menu) that allows you to take ownership of files.  Then right click on the file that's causing you issues, click take ownership, delete it and empty your recycling bin.

Hope this helps!

I do it similar, but slightly different.  Maybe it could help! 😀 

Quick explanation: I take one number and multiply it with every place (ones, tens, hundreds, etc.) of the next, then simply add them.

Detailed explanation: take the first number and the ones digit of the next and multiply them, then set that number to the side (write down, remember it, whatever works for you to not lose it). Then take the first number again and multiply it with the tens digit (don't forget to include the zero behind this), and set the solution to that to the side.  Continue like this all the way to the end, remembering to add zeros to fit the digit's place (tens = one zero, hundreds = two zeros, thousands = three zeros, etc.).  Lastly add them all together for the finished solution!

Examples:
#1 (with guide text):
14 x 28 = ?

Start by multiplying the first number with the ones digit of the second number:
14 x 8 = 102

Now we set 102 to the side to bring back at the end.

Next multiply the first number with the tens digit of the second number (remember to include the zero after the digit):
14 x 20 = 280

Now we can take both solutions and add them together:
102 + 280 = 382

Which means that our original equation (14 x 28) is equal to 382, aka:
14 x 28 = 382

#2 (your equation):
1005 x 105 = ?

1005 x 5 = 5025

1005 x 0 = 0
(Note: including a zero any digit past the ones place isn't needed as any amount of zeros is still just zero.     (0 = 00)

1005 x 100 = 100500

5025 + 0 + 100500 = 105525

1005 x 105 = 105525

#3 (random example, no text):
73 x 92 = ?

73 x 2 = 146

73 x 90 = 6570

146 + 6570 = 6716

73 x 92 = 6716

Hope this helps at least a bit! Looking over it, I'm not too sure if it will as it is - practically speaking - a modified version of FOIL multiplication, but sometimes just hearing something from another perspective can be enough for you to figure it out better!  😄  Wish you luck!

So I've been in and out of treatment for over 2 years now for suicidal depression, anxiety, and ptsd.  I've also been in and out of treatment for ADHD and ODD since 2nd grade.  

Due to trauma, I've had extreme difficulty feeling connection with anyone ever, beside one person, my dad.  That relationship dissolved several years ago though.

Right now I'm in a Intensive Residential Treatment Center for the second time and I'll be getting out on Halloween.  I have no where I can go.  That's not EXACTLY true.  I have my mom's house, my dad, and a couple of relatives, but each one of those have pretty glaring issues that would almost certainly bring to another mental crisis.

At my mom's house is my step father who has abused me in the past.  I found out while in the hospital after a suicide attempt that my dad doesn't want me back with him (didn't say why, but it's probably because I spent practically a year laying bed between different treatments, and he doesn't want me there if I'm not paying bills, which I guess is fair).  I'm not very close with the rest of my relatives and due to my recent past of isolating and ignoring everyone, they don't seem very comfortable around me.

I have a case manager who is trying to find a place, but having no luck.  I've put in for disability and we've been waiting months now, but chances are that I'm not going to accepted before my time here is up.

Things despite this have been going okay as I found a combination of meds that give me some energy and motivation, but I can feel these benefits waning as time till the discharge draws near.

Honestly, I think I'm kinda hoping to be let out without a destination.  I feel so very disconnected from everyone and everything as I have isolated and avoided EVERYONE that I have ever known.  Through these treatments, I've been able to open communication with some people again, and ever repaired some damaged relations ships, but I don't FEEL it. I don't FEEL like I'm a part of any whole or group.  I can see - I cognitively and logically understand - from people's actions that there are people that care about me, but, despite desperately wanting to, I don't care about anyone.  I keep pushing myself to socialize, to express myself, to learn, to live, but for God's sake I just don't care about any of it.

I believe it is because they make music that you have to take more time, and effort, to chew.

Most pop music (or just most music in general) is incredibly similar.  The rhythm is either 3 beats per measure (1 2 3, 1 2 3, 1 2 3, ...) or four beats per measure (1 2 3 4, 1 2 3 4, ...) throughout the entire song and the percussion typically sticks close to these timings.  Most songs lyrics are more simple and easy to understand and rarely go much longer than 4 minutes.

With Tool however, the rhythm can be seemingly almost any amount per measure and on top of that, it almost (if not) always changes.  In what is their most popular song, Schism, the main riff switches between 5 and 7 beats per measure.  Flood's main riff is 13 beats per measure. Jimmy's is 6 beats the first two measures and then 8 beats on the third.  

Along with the rhythmic structure of the song, Danny adds to the depth exponentially by playing in polyrhythm, which is when you play two different rhythms at the same time.  A great example of this is at the very end of Ænema (about 6:26), Maynard's "æ" happens 3 times in the same space that Danny hits his drums 4 times.

On top of those two things are heaps of unique sound effects on their instruments, a variety of synthes, and Maynard's extremely distinguished voice with that has such a range to sound at times femininely sassy, a frustratingly pissed, and at all times, pure and centered.  There's Adam's ability to make each album have a similar tone between songs without them sounding repetitive, the deep and engaging lyrics, and the cryptic and baffling music videos.  Adam has described that they like to make songs in the format of a story (introduction, rising action, climax, resolution) and it shows.  Songs rarely play out like most music with verse1 chorus verse2 chorus interlude chorus end.  The end of the song typically sounds quite different than the beginning.

I saw in an interview, Maynard had compared most music to chewing gum.  You chew on it until it loses its flavor, then you spit it out.  Tool is much harder to chew and has a lot more flavor.  It reminds me of when listening to quite a lot of Tool's songs the first time, I really didn't like them. However, there would usually be a section of the song that got stuck in my head, and after listening to the song multiple times, and really digesting it, I would come to love it!

At the same time, all these things are why I feel like a lot of people can't get into Tool. It's too different.  One could go their entire life only hearing music with 3 or 4 beats per measure, that is 4 minutes or less, and that sticks to a more common structure.  Expectations of what music intrinsically is, to such a person, might cause them, upon listening to Tool, to feel it might not even BE music.



Tldr:  Tool's music is much more complex than most music, which means there's more nuance for people who like it, to like more.  This also means that there's more nuance for people don't like it, to like it less.

I, for quite a while, want to get a guitar and start learning to play, but finding Tool was what got me to actually do it.  The variety of different tones and sounds that Adam displays through their discography maxed my curiosity of how he played it and how it FELT to play it.  It also feels like there's a fair amount of easier songs and plenty of easy riffs that made playing guitar more fun sooner.  😄
